scope: Broad Linux validation of the R42 branch head on the completion host; fixes for every failure found
head: 154ae474aa (work/r42-linux-acceptance; parent 8de4c5102d)

environment.compilers: Clang 22.1.8 (pinned CI Clang 23 unavailable on this host; documented, not substituted)
qt: offscreen for CTest, Xvfb 1920x1080 + xcb for functional journeys
environment.mold: 2.40.4 local extraction for the pinned sanitizer profile

fixes: Ported the R10 animation test switch: every QML Behavior and popup enter/exit Transition is gated by Theme.animationsEnabled; the QML, unit and integration mains, CTest environments and both functional harnesses default BITCOIN_QML_TEST_NO_ANIMATIONS=1; motion-asserting cases opt in; production keeps animations when the variable is unset

Sandboxed XDG_CONFIG_HOME for the whole unit-test binary: legacy-migration fixtures capture and verify external QSettings stores by organization/application name, so a real ~/.config/Bitcoin presence (a key serialized as @Invalid(), where contains() is true but the value is invalid) can never satisfy the capture contract, and unsandboxed writes polluted the machine across runs

Anchored the pinned Core signer mock with a compile-time absolute path: ctest starts the integration binary in a build subdirectory, so the __FILE__-relative traversal only worked when the build tree happened to sit three levels under the source root
Added the controls import that the gated ReceiveRequestModal transitions reference

Collect QtQml between MainRouting cases (gc() in cleanup after destruction receipts): an allocation-triggered full collection inside a later case crashed intermittently in QtQml GCStateMachine (SEGV writing through a corrupted QV4 array during runFullGC from allocString) on Qt 6.4.2 and 6.10.2, after the case assertions already passed. 20/20 clean full-suite runs on Qt 6.10.2 and 15/15 on Qt 6.4.2 where the crash previously reproduced within a handful of runs. Controlled-point collection, not an upstream root-cause claim
The coins amount-popup drag case opts into motion: with test motion disabled the settled scene stops producing frames and waitForRendering times out

Suppressed Qt QBitArray's qsizetype-to-byte narrowing (qbitarray.h:92) as a dependency exception next to the existing qhashfunctions.h entry; the pinned halt-on-error UBSan configuration halted the PsbtWork suite on that Qt-header diagnostic

Widened the wallet security-state QTRY budget to a shared 15 s constant in the integration fixture: under ASan the unlock/encrypt paths reported 150-300 ms over QtTest's 5 s default (QtTest named the sufficient margin). Assertions unchanged; all six previously failing ASan integration groups pass

Kept motion enabled inside the integration child journeys (qunsetenv in the integration runner main): integration cases drive the complete application before and after the child re-exec, and with instant transitions the shutdown visibility cascade crashed Qt Quick's teardown binding on 6.4.2/6.10.2. The send manual-sweep case crashed 7/8 with motion off and passes 10/10 with motion on. Component QML suites keep motion disabled via the ctest environment

asan_host_environment_notes.wrapper: ci/with_sanitizer_env.py applies Core's pinned ASan/LSan/UBSan options with the combined app suppressions
asan_host_environment_notes.ubsan: Core's random.h shift and sha256 overflow diagnostics are suppressed only when llvm-symbolizer is on PATH (the pinned CI images carry it); without symbolization the function-name suppressions cannot match and halt_on_error kills the children
asan_host_environment_notes.lsan: This host's desktop stack (NVIDIA GL, session DBus, X11) leaks at exit inside system libraries; every reported leak stack is in those libraries with zero application frames. The pinned CI containers do not load them. With the symbolizer enabled, LSan suppression matching on this host cannot match the stripped Qt/system module frames, so the full ASan run disables leak detection for this environment noise; ASan memory-error detection and UBSan halting remain fully active; the suppression-control test itself still runs with LSan enabled and passes
asan_host_environment_notes.stale_binary_note: An intermediate ASan binary built incrementally across the fix commits reported 16 BackupPolicy failures; a clean parent+head rebuild passes 146/146 for that class at both revisions, isolating the report to stale incremental artifacts rather than source
